title: Meta prompting
caption: A separate session writes the context for you: the AI asks, you answer, and the bench gets one clean work order.

exchange.a2: The front desk, by phone and walk-in.

users-answer-better-than-they-write.header: Users answer better than they write
users-answer-better-than-they-write.description: when a model elicits preferences with open-ended questions, the user's answers are often more informative than prompts they wrote unaided, and users report it takes less effort [1].

li-eliciting-human-preferences.title: Li et al., Eliciting Human Preferences with Language Models

prompts-generated-from-requirements.description: REprompt builds a multi-agent prompt optimizer from requirements-engineering principles; the abstract reports effective optimization without numbers, and it is an early preprint [1].

shi-reprompt.title: Shi, Sun, Chen, Wu, Chen, Jin, Liu, REprompt: Prompt Generation for Intelligent Software Development Guided by Requirements Engineering

separate-session.title: Separate session
separate-session.script: Meta prompting means using one AI chat to write the brief for another. The separate session creates the context for you, and it should be high-signal: the smallest set of what matters, enough to get the job done and nothing that drags it down.

fresh-chat-clean-work-order.title: Fresh chat, clean work order
fresh-chat-clean-work-order.script: Then take the result into a fresh chat instead of continuing the long one. The bench is where the AI’s context sits, and it gets one clean work order, not the whole conversation that led to it.

why-a-separate-office.title: Why a separate office
why-a-separate-office.script: Why a separate office? Because the planning chat is full of questions, half-ideas and drafts, and in the bench's terms that is rot. The work order is not. So keep the office and the bench apart.
